source.title: AAOIFI Governance Standard (GS) 1 (Revised 2024) - Shari'ah Governance Framework

display_card: GS 1 (Revised 2024): Shari'ah Governance Framework - overarching 14-principle framework covering RSAs, CSB, SSB, compliance function, internal/external Shari'ah audit, TCWG and senior management roles
applicability: Applies to all IFIs, including Islamic finance windows, across all sectors (para 2).

RSAs may choose to apply to other institutions in their jurisdictions as appropriate; applies insofar as practicable to non-IFI institutions adopting AAOIFI GSs, including social finance institutions (para 2).
Also applies to external stakeholders of institutions (including RSAs) to the extent of their responsibilities defined in this standard (para 3).
Acts as centre-point standard complementing multiple other AAOIFI governance standards and guidance (PR5, footnote 1).
core_machinery: 14 Principles (paras 5-18 summary; detailed at paras 19-81): 1) Shari'ah governance framework; 2) role of RSAs; 3) central Shari'ah board; 4) unique organs (SSB, Shari'ah compliance function, internal Shari'ah audit, external Shari'ah audit); 5) role of TCWG and senior management; 6) SSB; 7) Shari'ah compliance function; 8) internal Shari'ah audit function; 9) external Shari'ah audit; 10) Islamic finance windows; 11) Islamic finance subsidiaries/associates; 12) business model/stakeholder considerations; 13) applicability to different sectors; 14) transparency and disclosure.

TCWG roles/responsibilities (paras 36-46): policy approval, oversight of CSB/SSB rulings implementation, internal control oversight, senior management performance oversight, corporate culture; capacity development; interaction with SSB; ensuring SSB independence and resourcing; annual SSB performance assessment (administrative only).

Senior management roles/responsibilities (paras 47-51): implementing framework, management structure/reporting, implementing CSB/SSB rulings, communication policy, capacity building, cooperation with SSB/other organs, SSB secretariat appointment and functions.

Sector-specific application: Islamic Capital Market (ICM) requirements (paras 68-72), Islamic microfinance/fintech/financial inclusion flexibility (paras 73-75), Takaful-specific disclosures (paras 80-81).
Transparency and disclosure requirements including Zakah and charity fund disclosures (paras 76-79).
implications: Mandatory minimum organs of institutional Shari'ah governance: SSB, Shari'ah compliance function, internal Shari'ah audit function, external Shari'ah audit (para 8).

External Shari'ah audit (ESA) becomes mandatory for 'public interest institutions' (listed institutions, institutions with publicly traded securities e.g. Sukuk, retail IFIs with >10,000 stakeholders) three years after the effective date; strongly recommended for all others in the interim (paras 55-56, definition para 4h).

TCWG may perform only administrative assessment of SSB performance/effectiveness - not substantive assessment, and senior management cannot perform SSB assessment at all (para 44 and its explanation).
CSB establishment remains a 'recommended' (not mandatory or strongly recommended) practice for RSAs/governments (para 7, BC21-23).

For ICM, SSB must comprise three or more Shari'ah scholars, or be sourced via external Shari'ah consultancy firm meeting fit-and-proper/governance criteria; CSB requirements (where they exist) prevail (para 70).
Proportionality principle allows flexible application based on institution size, business model, and jurisdictional development stage (para 62).
limitations: Institutions may outsource specific components of the Shari'ah governance framework subject to TCWG approval and due diligence (para 63); however GS 9 separately prohibits outsourcing of the SCD specifically.
Regulatory flexibility permitted for microfinance/fintech/financial-inclusion organizations, e.g. allowing single-member SSBs or shared SSBs (paras 73-75).
ESA mandate applies only to public interest institutions after a 3-year transition; not universally mandatory (para 56, BC15b-c).
CSB formation kept as 'recommended' rather than 'strongly recommended' after public consultation pushback (BC22-23).
disputes: BC1-BC3: choice of principle-based (with prescriptive elements where needed) vs rule-based standard development approach.

BC4-BC9: defining the Shari'ah principles and rules hierarchy - debate on whether to centralize the hierarchy vs leaving to RSAs/Ijtihad; concluded a defined hierarchy is essential for global uniformity.
BC10: inclusion of RSA responsibilities within the standard as an exception, given RSAs' role as key external stakeholders.
BC11-BC13: balancing quality of Shari'ah governance framework against cost to institutions; proportionality, optional/preferred vs mandatory provisions, and transition periods used to optimize cost.

BC14-BC15: whether/when external Shari'ah audit (ESA) should be mandatory; concluded mandatory only for public interest institutions after 3-year transition, with minimum requirements retained in this standard despite AAOIFI SOAA 6 covering ESA conduct in detail.
BC16-BC20: applicability of Shari'ah governance framework to overseas branches/subsidiaries of IFIs, including cases of differing RSA approaches to AAOIFI GS adoption across jurisdictions.
BC21-BC23: level of emphasis for CSB establishment recommendation - moved from proposed 'strongly recommended' back down to 'recommended' after public consultation and PIMCC feedback.
BC24: quality assurance of external Shari'ah auditors/service providers - deemed out of scope for this standard, left to respective RSAs.

timeline_bridge.effective_date: On or after 1 January 2026 (para 82); earlier application encouraged
timeline_bridge.history: Originated from joint IFSB-AAOIFI exposure draft 'Revised Shari'ah Governance Framework for Institutions Offering Islamic Financial Services' issued 16 Ramadan 1444H / 7 April 2022 (H1); AAOIFI subsequently proceeded independently (H2); AGEB approved working group 28 August 2023 (H3); exposure draft issued 25 December 2023 (H6); public hearings Jan-Jul 2024 (H7); PIMCC review 30 April 2024 (H8); Shari'ah Board's Committee reviews through Nov 2024 (H9); finalised and approved 20-22 May 2024, issued as final 29 December 2024 (H11).
timeline_bridge.adoption: Approved in AAOIFI Governance and Ethics Board meeting No. 37, 12-14 Dhul-Qa'dah 1445H / 20-22 May 2024 (Appendix A)
